meta.storyTitle: Isolate reviewer access and fetch dependency advisories

summary.prose: This Story checks a repository's dependencies against public advisories. The reviewer runs with the SAME host access as the controller itself -- no sandboxing or egress/filesystem restriction is attempted, since constraining the reviewer would degrade the review's own accuracy. s2 computes one deterministic content identity over the COMPLETE transitive closure of each manager's required inputs (not just the top-level manifest -- a requirements file's own nested -r/-c references, and a go module's full source tree, all participate), re-verifies that identity immediately after every manager's audit completes, and stamps contentStable so s3 can tell a stable collection from one a concurrent edit (even one restored before s3 checks) touched mid-run. Each package manager is pointed at the repository's own actual, LOCKED dependencies -- never an ambient environment or a stale, loosely-constrained file that could mask a vulnerable pinned version. Every manager's CONFIGURED destination (never claimed as independently observed) is recorded per manager, including for a clean, zero-finding or failed run, not only when a match is found. A manager, dependency or source that cannot be correctly targeted or resolved is reported as an explicit gap.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: The Epic adds a standalone orchestration module (outside src/workflow/review-round/) that owns model selection, dependency-advisory collection, code-assessment execution, and reporting, and supplies review-round's existing RoundDriverHooks.security hook as a thin adapter. review-round itself stays unchanged except for the one call site invoking that hook; the data shapes it already exports (SecurityFinding, SecurityLocator, EvidenceProvider, VerificationReceipt) are populated, never redefined.

ownedContracts.name: SecurityAdvisoryEvidence
ownedContracts.purpose: Carries s2's dependency-advisory collection outcome (controller-side, no model) across the boundary: the pinned contentIdentity it was collected against (so s3 can verify it recomputes/matches the same identity before trusting this evidence), whether that identity stayed stable across s2's own collection run (contentStable), the queried coordinates, the actual advisory matches with affected versions and provenance, the per-manager CONFIGURED destination (never claimed as independently observed), the per-manager input mode used (manifest-scoped | isolated-environment | confined-source-copy | unsupported, retained as a correctness/targeting concern, not an isolation one), and the dependencies/sources that stayed unresolved, unavailable or unsupported -- so s3 can report confirmed affected dependencies and unverified coverage as DISTINCT values bound to the SAME content identity as its own code findings.

boundary.internal: pkg_audit's package-manager resolution; s2 runs with the SAME host access as the controller itself -- no network or filesystem sandboxing is attempted. s2 records, per manager, its CONFIGURED destination and stamps contentStable from a post-audit re-verification (observability + a bounded mutation check, not enforcement); the documented per-manager input/mode mapping is retained as a CORRECTNESS/targeting requirement, with an explicit coverage gap for any manager s2 cannot correctly target under that mapping; and the advisory-match collection that populates SecurityAdvisoryEvidence (stamped with the pinned contentIdentity, computed by hashing the COMPLETE TRANSITIVE closure of required input bytes directly) stay private to s2. s2 is responsible only for the dependency-manifest closure its own contentIdentity covers; ensuring the caller's targets.entries also covers what s3's code pass needs reviewed is the ORCHESTRATOR's responsibility, not s2's -- s2 neither expands into application source nor second-guesses targets.entries' completeness beyond its own manifest closure. No model, tool-loop, or CLI session is involved in s2 at all. ac2's gap-reporting distinguishes a SUCCESSFUL audit that found vulnerabilities from an EXECUTION GAP -- these are never conflated.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Model-tier resolution (extending src/config/role-taxonomy.ts with a security role), availability/credential checks, and the no-silent-fallback blocker-reporting logic stay private to s1; only the resolved SecurityModelSelection crosses its boundary. s1 must also specify the configuration contract for an INDEPENDENTLY selectable security-model binding (distinct from core/mid/cheap) and its interaction with coreFloor enforcement and unavailable-model handling; this is s1's central, still-open design question.

The RoundDriverHooks.security adapter function; the CliProvider.runReadOnlySession dispatch of the code-vulnerability pass against the SAME pinned contentIdentity s2 collected against (recomputed/verified by s3, refusing on a content MISMATCH or on sc2.contentStable=false), using s1's resolved model, with the SAME host access every other CLI-backed session in this codebase already has. The call into runReviewRound and the separate ownership of everything runReviewRound itself does NOT do (sandbox/mutation checkpoint execution, round reconciliation, VerificationReceipt persistence, and checkpoint cleanup); the mapping from the review's pinned contentIdentity onto the epicHash/storyId identity persistVerificationReceipt requires; the OWNERSHIP of ensuring targets.entries' scope covers everything both s2's dependency closure and s3's own code-review pass need (s2 only computes contentIdentity over its own manifest closure, never app source); and the assembly of SecurityFinding/SecurityEvidence plus a supplemental report structure stay private to s3. It consumes s1's SecurityModelSelection and s2's SecurityAdvisoryEvidence to produce that report.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase A -- foundational contracts (model selection and dependency-advisory collection)

nonFunctional.security: s2 and s3 run with the SAME host access as the controller itself -- neither attempts network or filesystem confinement. s2 records, per manager, its CONFIGURED destination (never claimed as observed) and a contentStable flag from its own post-audit re-verification; these are observability + a bounded correctness check, not an enforced boundary, and neither is a basis for refusing to run a manager (a manager is refused only when it cannot be correctly TARGETED, or when contentStable comes back false). s2's per-manager input/mode mapping is retained as a CORRECTNESS requirement. s3's code-vulnerability pass is dispatched through CliProvider.runReadOnlySession with the same access level every other CLI-backed session in this codebase already has. contentIdentity is computed over the COMPLETE TRANSITIVE closure of each manager's required inputs (a requirements file's own nested -r/-c references; a go module's full source tree) by hashing actual bytes directly and unconditionally -- never inferred from git status alone. s2 re-verifies this identity immediately after its own collection completes and stamps contentStable; s3 separately recomputes and verifies the identity before trusting s2's evidence, refusing on an actual content mismatch OR on contentStable=false.
nonFunctional.observability: Every checkpoint run -- pass or fail, whether or not a SecurityFinding corroborates it -- is recorded as a VerificationReceipt (already built, src/workflow/review-round/receipt-record.ts), so a security review's execution is auditable independent of its findings. s3 owns stamping that record with the epicHash/storyId persistVerificationReceipt requires, mapped from the review's own pinned contentIdentity. s2's per-manager configuredDestination and contentStable fields (see nonFunctional.security) are the equivalent audit trail for the dependency-advisory pass, persisted per manager even for a clean or failed run, not only when a match is found.
nonFunctional.durability: No new persistent storage is introduced for s1/s2's own outputs (SecurityModelSelection, SecurityAdvisoryEvidence are transient per-review values); the durable records are the already-typed SecurityFinding/VerificationReceipt heads the shared round-driver machinery (Epic 03f4fd3b9102aab8) persists, plus s3's new supplemental report structure (not yet a stored artifact type; its persistence mechanism is an open question for the s3 LLD).
nonFunctional.performance: Not a stated constraint for this Epic; the new module's cost is bounded by one pkg_audit invocation (per targeted manager) plus one re-verification hash pass, and one CLI read-only session per request, not a new background job.

api.name: computeContentIdentity
api.signature: function computeContentIdentity(repoPath: string, targets: ReviewTargets): Promise<string>

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: The registered repo root git_rev_parse runs against, and the base every targets.entries path is resolved and validated against.

parameters.name: targets
parameters.purpose: The round's submitter-owned content list; computeContentIdentity expands each manager's COMPLETE TRANSITIVE required-input closure around these entries -- including a requirements file's own nested -r/-c references and, for go, the module's full source tree -- not just the single top-level manifest path named.

returns.meaning: A deterministic digest over the repo's HEAD commit sha (via git_rev_parse) plus a sha256 (Node's own crypto) of EVERY file in the complete, transitively-closed required-input set's actual, current raw bytes -- read and hashed unconditionally, never gated on git status. Called twice by collectDependencyAdvisories (once before, once immediately after running every manager's audit) to detect a mutation during the collection window; s3 separately recomputes it again before trusting the evidence.

errors.condition: the target repository's git state cannot be read (not a git repository, repoPath not registered, or the underlying git_rev_parse call fails)
a targets.entries path resolves outside repoPath
a nested -r/-c reference inside a required requirements file cannot be resolved (missing or unreadable)

preconditions: repoPath is a registered repo root with a resolvable HEAD
postconditions: pure function of the repo's current file bytes, repoPath and targets.entries -- calling it twice with no intervening change to the complete, transitively-closed input set yields the identical string
follows every nested -r/-c reference inside a pip-family requirements file, and includes a go module's full source tree, not just its manifest/lockfile pair
never includes file content from outside repoPath or the complete required-input closure
hashes raw file bytes directly -- never delegates to git_hash_object or relies on git status to decide which files to include

api.name: collectDependencyAdvisories
api.signature: function collectDependencyAdvisories(repoPath: string, targets: ReviewTargets): Promise<SecurityAdvisoryEvidence>

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: Same registered repo root as computeContentIdentity; also the root enumerateManagers walks to find every manifest in scope.

parameters.name: targets
parameters.purpose: Bounds which manifests/managers are in scope for this collection, same as computeContentIdentity's targets.

returns.meaning: sc2's full result: contentIdentity (computed BEFORE running any manager's audit), contentStable (true iff a SECOND computeContentIdentity call made immediately after every manager's audit completes returns the identical string), queriedCoordinates, matches, perManagerMode (each entry now carrying configuredDestination), unresolvedDependencies, and unavailableSources.

preconditions: enumerateManagers(repoPath, targets) has found at least an attempt-worthy manifest, or the result is an all-gaps SecurityAdvisoryEvidence
postconditions: computes contentIdentity once before any manager runs, then again immediately after the LAST manager's audit completes; contentStable is false whenever these two values differ, surfacing a mutation that happened during collection (including one restored before s3's own later check) rather than silently trusting the pre-audit value
every manager it attempts runs with the SAME host access as the controller itself, directly against repoPath (or the manager's own manifest directory within it) -- no sandboxing, no isolated copy

every manager is correctly TARGETED at its own locked/pinned dependencies (never an ambient default, and never a stale or loosely-constrained file that could mask a vulnerable pinned version): pipenv/poetry ALWAYS regenerate their requirements input fresh from Pipfile.lock/poetry.lock, ignoring any stray requirements.txt that might sit beside them; plain pip uses its own existing requirements.txt directly (no lockfile alternative exists for bare pip)
records, per manager, the configuredDestination it was set up to reach -- persisted on EVERY perManagerMode entry, including a manager that found nothing or failed, not only one that produced a match
every queried coordinate ends up in exactly one of matches or unresolvedDependencies -- never silently dropped
never throws -- every manager-level failure becomes an explicit perManagerMode/unavailableSources/unresolvedDependencies entry, not an exception, matching ac2's 'remain explicit gaps' requirement

api.name: createDependencySbomEvidenceProvider

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: Captured in the returned provider's closure and forwarded to collectDependencyAdvisories on every run() call, since EvidenceProvider.run's own fixed signature carries no repo-identity field.

returns.meaning: An object with category:'dependency-sbom' whose run(input) calls collectDependencyAdvisories(repoPath, input.targets) and maps its matches into the thin EvidenceProviderOutput.evidence. The richer SecurityAdvisoryEvidence itself is NOT part of this return value -- the orchestration module obtains sc2 directly by calling collectDependencyAdvisories.

postconditions: the returned object satisfies the EvidenceProvider interface exactly, so the existing EvidenceProviderRegistry can hold it under the 'dependency-sbom' key unchanged

dataModelChanges.entity: pkgAuditTool inputSchema + execute -- new optional requirementsPath field
dataModelChanges.details: Add one optional `requirementsPath?: string` property to pkgAuditTool's inputSchema. auditArgv's pip/pipenv/poetry cases append `-r <requirementsPath>` to the pip-audit invocation when it is provided; when it is OMITTED, every manager's behavior is byte-for-byte identical to today (pip-audit's ambient-environment default, pipenv's own `pipenv check`, poetry's own `poetry audit`) -- this is the mechanism that replaces revision-3's unspecified 'field-modify', making the change purely additive and leaving every existing caller (including one that omits the field) unaffected. s2 is the only caller that ever passes it.

dataModelChanges.entity: requirementsPath generation + lifecycle (precedence rule, concurrency-safe temp file)
dataModelChanges.details: For pipenv/poetry: ALWAYS regenerate a fresh requirements-shaped file directly from Pipfile.lock/poetry.lock's own pinned {name, version} pairs -- a stray requirements.txt sitting beside either lockfile is never consulted, so it can never mask a locked vulnerable version with a looser or stale constraint. For plain pip: use the repository's own existing requirements.txt directly via requirementsPath (no generation, since there is no lockfile to regenerate from); a plain pip project with no requirements.txt at all is an explicit coverage gap (see error paths), never a fallback to the ambient environment. Any generated file is written to a per-call-unique temp path (os.tmpdir() + a fresh random id, never a fixed or shared filename) and removed in a finally block once pkg_audit returns -- so two concurrent collectDependencyAdvisories calls (different repos, or the same repo audited twice) never collide on the same generated file.

CURRENT INVARIANT BEING REPLACED (revision 3): requiredInputsForManager named only each manager's top-level manifest + lockfile pair (e.g. go -> {go.mod, go.sum}), which computeContentIdentity hashed directly -- missing a pip-family requirements file's own nested `-r other.txt` / `-c constraints.txt` references (which DO affect what pip-audit actually resolves and audits), and missing the rest of a go module's source tree (which govulncheck's source-level, call-graph analysis DOES consume beyond go.mod/go.sum). NEW behavior: the required-input resolver follows every nested -r/-c reference inside a pip-family requirements file recursively, and for go, walks the full module's own source tree (every .go file under the module root, following the module boundary govulncheck itself respects) -- all of it participates in computeContentIdentity's hash, not just the top-level manifest/lockfile pair.

collectDependencyAdvisories calls computeContentIdentity ONCE before running any manager's audit, and ONCE MORE immediately after the last manager's audit completes, over the identical repoPath/targets. contentStable is true only when both calls return the identical string. This does not eliminate every possible mutation-during-audit race (a change-and-restore occurring entirely within the narrow window between the two calls would still go undetected), but it closes the much larger window the revision-3/-2 designs left open -- a change made and restored at ANY point before s3's own later check would previously go undetected entirely; now it is caught unless it happens to land inside s2's own, much shorter collection window.

dataModelChanges.entity: configuredDestination recording (replaces the revision-3 'destination actually reached' framing)
dataModelChanges.details: pkg_audit's own output (manager, exitCode, parsed, stdout, stderr -- pkg/index.ts's PkgAuditData) carries no independent network trace, so s2 cannot claim to OBSERVE which destination a manager's traffic actually reached. Instead, s2 records each manager's CONFIGURED destination -- the registry/index/advisory-source that manager's own configuration (its default, or any explicit override s2 set up) names -- and labels it honestly as configured, never observed. This is attached to EVERY perManagerMode entry (one per manager attempted), so the audit trail survives a clean, zero-finding run or a failed one, not only a run that produced a match.

dataModelChanges.entity: Repository-root threading (repoPath) through computeContentIdentity, collectDependencyAdvisories, createDependencySbomEvidenceProvider
dataModelChanges.details: ReviewTargets carries no repository identity, so a relative path like package.json is ambiguous across two registered repos sharing that relative path. Every s2-owned function takes an explicit repoPath; every targets.entries path is validated as resolving inside repoPath before use.

dataModelChanges.entity: enumerateManagers (replaces reliance on detectManager's single-match precedence)
dataModelChanges.details: detectManager(cwd) returns only the FIRST manager it finds via a fixed lockfile precedence order -- it never enumerates co-located managers or nested project directories. enumerateManagers(repoPath, targets) walks every manifest/lockfile signal within repoPath bounded by targets.entries' own directories, producing one {manager, manifestDir} pair per manifest found; two conflicting manifests in the SAME directory for the SAME manager family are flagged as an unresolved ambiguity rather than guessed at.

Translates each manager's own result shape into the common SecurityAdvisoryMatch[] shape. An unparseable or malformed result is recorded in unavailableSources as an execution gap, never silently treated as 'no findings'.

The HLD-defined output record this Story owns (HLD revision 6): { contentIdentity, contentStable, readOnly: true, queriedCoordinates, matches: SecurityAdvisoryMatch[], perManagerMode (each entry carrying an optional configuredDestination), unresolvedDependencies, unavailableSources }. Lives in the Epic's new standalone orchestration module, and crosses the s2->s3 boundary unchanged.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: collectDependencyAdvisories is the sole producer of SecurityAdvisoryEvidence. It computes contentIdentity over the complete transitive required-input closure BEFORE running any manager, correctly targets each manager at its own locked dependencies, runs pkg_audit with controller-equivalent access, records each manager's configuredDestination, recomputes contentIdentity once more AFTER every manager completes to stamp contentStable, and maps each manager's output into SecurityAdvisoryMatch[]. Every unresolved/unavailable/unsupported case is recorded explicitly. s3 consumes the returned value directly to recompute and verify contentIdentity before trusting the evidence, refusing on a mismatch or on contentStable=false, and to report confirmed affected dependencies vs. unverified coverage as distinct values in its own report.

errorCases.scenario: The repository's content changes between s2's pre-audit and post-audit contentIdentity computations (e.g. a required input file is edited during a long-running audit, whether or not it is restored afterward).
errorCases.detection: collectDependencyAdvisories's second computeContentIdentity call (run immediately after the last manager's audit) returns a different string than the first.
errorCases.response: SecurityAdvisoryEvidence.contentStable is set to false; the evidence is still returned (not discarded), but s3 is contractually required to treat contentStable=false as untrustworthy and refuse rather than silently use it.
errorCases.userImpact: A mutation during collection -- even one restored before any later check would otherwise have seen it -- is caught and surfaced, rather than silently trusted.

errorCases.scenario: A nested -r/-c reference inside a required requirements file cannot be resolved (the referenced file is missing, unreadable, or itself points outside the expected project scope).
errorCases.detection: The required-input closure resolver's recursive walk fails to read the referenced file.
errorCases.response: That manager's perManagerMode is recorded 'unsupported' -- the manager is never audited against an incomplete closure, and contentIdentity is never computed over a partial, silently-truncated input set.
errorCases.userImpact: Never silently audits (or hashes) less than the real, complete dependency closure.

errorCases.scenario: Writing or removing the generated requirementsPath temp file fails (disk full, permissions, or the finally-block cleanup itself errors).
errorCases.detection: The fs write/unlink call surfaces an error.
errorCases.response: That manager's perManagerMode is recorded 'unavailable'/'unsupported'; pkg_audit is never invoked with a missing or stale generated file.
errorCases.userImpact: Never runs an audit against a file that may not actually contain what was intended.

errorCases.scenario: pkg_audit's underlying CLI binary is not installed for a manager enumerateManagers found (e.g. pip-audit itself is missing).
errorCases.detection: runShell's existing r.spawnError flag surfaces back to collectDependencyAdvisories.
errorCases.response: That manager is recorded in unavailableSources as an execution gap, never conflated with 'no findings reported'.
errorCases.userImpact: Distinguishes 'the audit tool is genuinely absent' from 'the audit ran and found nothing.'

errorCases.scenario: A manager's audit output is unparseable or malformed, distinct from pkg_audit's normal nonZeroOk:true 'findings reported' convention.
errorCases.detection: The per-manager raw-output-to-SecurityAdvisoryMatch mapper fails to extract any usable fields from r.stdout.
errorCases.response: Recorded in unavailableSources as an execution gap; never silently reported as a clean, findings-free result.
errorCases.userImpact: A parse failure never masquerades as a successful security check.

errorCases.scenario: A plain `pip` project has no requirements.txt at all -- there is nothing to point pip-audit's `-r` argument at, and plain pip has no lockfile alternative to generate one from.
errorCases.detection: requiredInputsForManager finds no requirements-shaped file for the detected pip project.
errorCases.response: Recorded as perManagerMode 'unsupported' -- never falls back to auditing the ambient active environment.
errorCases.userImpact: Never silently reverts to the wrong (ambient) target just because the expected file is missing.

errorCases.scenario: Two different package-manager manifests for the SAME manager family are found in the same directory under repoPath.
errorCases.detection: enumerateManagers detects more than one candidate manifest for the same manager family in one directory.
errorCases.response: That directory's manager is recorded as an unresolved ambiguity, never guessed at by picking one arbitrarily.
errorCases.userImpact: Never silently audits the wrong lockfile when two plausible ones exist.

edgeCases.input: A manager's audit legitimately exits non-zero with a fully parseable 'findings reported' result.
edgeCases.expected: Treated as a SUCCESSFUL audit -- matches populated from the parsed result, NOT an execution gap.

edgeCases.input: A requirements.txt contains `-r base.txt` and `-c constraints.txt`.
edgeCases.expected: Both referenced files are resolved into the hashed required-input set and into whatever pip-audit itself reads when given the top-level file via -r; neither is silently excluded from contentIdentity.

edgeCases.input: A .go source file (not go.mod/go.sum) is edited, with the module's declared dependencies unchanged.
edgeCases.expected: contentIdentity changes, because the full module source tree -- not just go.mod/go.sum -- participates in the hash.

edgeCases.input: A poetry project has a stray, stale requirements.txt sitting beside poetry.lock (e.g. left over from a prior tool).
edgeCases.expected: The stray requirements.txt is never consulted; s2 always regenerates its own requirements input fresh from poetry.lock's exact pinned versions for this manager.

edgeCases.input: The same coordinate name happens to appear via two different managers in two different directories in the same review.
edgeCases.expected: Each manager's match is recorded independently in matches, keyed by its own manager-scoped coordinate; no de-duplication.

edgeCases.input: A tracked requirements/lockfile is marked assume-unchanged and its real on-disk content has diverged from HEAD; git status reports nothing.
edgeCases.expected: computeContentIdentity still reflects the change -- it reads and hashes every required input file's actual current bytes directly, never consulting git status.

alternativesConsidered.name: Minimal additive pkg_audit env override + per-call ephemeral allowlisting proxy
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add one optional `env` field to pkgAuditTool's existing inputSchema (cwd is already there), forwarded to runShell's own per-call env option; s2's orchestration module starts a short-lived allowlisting proxy and per-manager scoped cwd/env for exactly the duration of one audit call.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add one optional `requirementsPath?: string` field to pkgAuditTool's inputSchema (purely additive -- omitted, every manager behaves exactly as today); auditArgv's pip/pipenv/poetry cases append `-r <requirementsPath>` only when it is provided. s2's own module: (1) computes contentIdentity over the COMPLETE TRANSITIVE required-input closure (following nested -r/-c references; a go module's full source tree) before running any manager; (2) enumerates every manager in scope, regenerating a fresh requirementsPath from Pipfile.lock/poetry.lock for pipenv/poetry (never a stray requirements.txt) or using plain pip's own requirements.txt directly, written to a per-call-unique temp file cleaned up in a finally block; (3) runs pkg_audit with the same host access the controller has; (4) records each manager's configuredDestination (honestly labeled as configured, never observed), persisted per manager even for a clean or failed run; (5) recomputes contentIdentity once more after the last manager completes and stamps contentStable; (6) maps pkg_audit's raw output into SecurityAdvisoryMatch[], and (7) wraps the result into both the thin EvidenceProviderOutput and the richer SecurityAdvisoryEvidence (sc2, now additionally carrying contentStable and perManagerMode[].configuredDestination per HLD revision 6). Revision 4 closes the TOCTOU/incomplete-closure/unobservable-destination/unspecified-wiring gaps the revision-3 reviewer found, without reintroducing any sandboxing; the choice of a1 over a2/a3 stands unchanged.
pros: Reuses pkg_audit directly -- the only code change is pointing pip-family managers at the repo's own requirements via -r, satisfying ac2's 'not a new fetcher' requirement
No proxy, isolation, or verification machinery to build or maintain -- the reviewer runs with the same host access as the controller, per the HLD's revision-5 policy
Full, accurate resolution (no --no-deps/--require-hashes restriction) is preferred over a restricted one now that sandboxing is explicitly out of scope
cons: s2's own reports of which destination each manager reached are self-reported by the native tool, not independently verified -- an accepted, documented tradeoff (HLD risky bit 'Controller-equivalent access tradeoff'), not a gap this Story tries to close

alternativesConsidered.name: A wholly separate scoped-audit fetcher bypassing pkg_audit
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Build a new, standalone dependency-advisory fetcher that duplicates argv-building and subprocess invocation for each manager itself, instead of calling pkgAuditTool at all.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Write a new module that re-implements per-manager argv construction (duplicating auditArgv's logic, which is module-private and not exported from pkg/index.ts) and calls runShell directly with full control over cwd/env/proxy from the start, never touching pkgAuditTool's existing execute() path.
pros: Total control over every invocation detail from the first line, no coordination with pkg_audit's existing input/output shape at all
cons: Directly violates ac2's explicit text: 'implemented as the EvidenceProvider registry's dependency-sbom category wired to the existing pkg_audit tool ..., not a new fetcher' -- this alternative IS a new fetcher
Duplicates per-manager argv logic (auditArgv) that already exists and is already correct, doubling the maintenance surface for npm/pnpm/yarn/pip/pipenv/poetry/go/cargo argument shapes
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates ac2's explicit text outright by being exactly the 'new fetcher' the Story forbids, and duplicates auditArgv's already-correct per-manager logic -- rejected regardless of its other merits.

alternativesConsidered.name: Mutate the daemon's own process.env around the pkg_audit call
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Avoid changing pkg_audit's code at all by temporarily overwriting process.env.HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY (and restoring it afterward) for the duration of the call, since pkgAuditTool.execute defaults to process.env when no env override is passed.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Before calling pkgAuditTool.execute, set process.env.HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY to the ephemeral proxy's address and the manager's scoped settings; restore the prior values in a finally block after the call returns.
pros: Zero changes to pkg_audit's own source at all
cons: process.env is GLOBAL to the daemon's Node process, which the daemon's own threaded/session architecture runs concurrent, unrelated shell-backed tool calls inside (per the project's daemon.threads design) -- a security review's proxy env could leak onto, or be clobbered by, a completely unrelated concurrent shell call in the same process, a correctness and isolation hazard a1's per-call options.env entirely avoids

A restore-in-finally still has a window where a concurrent call on another async task sees the mutated environment, since Node's single-threaded event loop interleaves awaits -- this is not a theoretical risk given the daemon already runs many concurrent tool calls per session
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Nominally keeps ac2's wiring intact (same pkgAuditTool.execute call site, no schema change) but the enforcement mechanism itself is unsafe under the daemon's own concurrent, threaded session model -- a global process.env mutation is not a boundary sc2's 'enforced, not merely observed' advisoryDestination can rely on. Moot at revision 3 since no env-based network enforcement of any kind is attempted anymore, but a1's per-call scoping remains the better code-change pattern regardless.
